clue.text: Antipodean creature needing bill cut back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the whole run of bill-then-cut from right to left

parts.note: a bar bill or account is a tab
to cut grass is to mow it

explanation.surface: An Australian animal is in need of a trimmed beak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TAB + MOW as one run, giving WOM + BAT.
explanation.definitionFit: This burrowing marsupial lives only in Australia, the Antipodes to British eyes.

clue.text: House where roof half taken up after snakes found

indicators.note: after places the reversed fragment behind the snakes synonym

parts.note: to snake is to wind, as a river winds

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
half of the four-letter word roof is its first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone describes a house whose roof was half lifted once snakes turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps the first two letters of ROOF, 'taken up' reads them upwards, and 'after' puts them behind the snakes word. 'House' is a royal dynasty, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The British royal family has been the House of Windsor since 1917.

clue.text: North central state nominates lunatic

indicators.note: lunatic means crazy, so the letters of nominates go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A Midwestern state puts forward someone mad as a candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lunatic' shuffles NOMINATES into the state name.
explanation.definitionFit: This US state lies in the upper Midwest, on the northern border of the country's middle.

clue.text: Semi-foolish taken in by goddess, clever

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside the goddess's name

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

indicators.note: semi- means half, so only the first half of the foolish synonym is kept

parts.note: foolish means stupid

explanation.surface: Someone half daft is fooled by a goddess, yet still canny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Semi-' keeps the first half of STUPID, and 'taken in by' sets it inside the Greek goddess's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute and clever are synonyms for sharp-witted.

clue.text: Shortage in attack — or in power?

definitions.text: Shortage in attack — or in power?

indicators.note: in places the shortage word inside the attack word

parts.note: a bout is an attack or fit, as of illness
a shortage is a lack

explanation.surface: A question of whether something is missing in an assault or in electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: LACK goes 'in' BOUT; read as a whole, the clue describes a shortage in power, a blackout.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackout is a failure of electricity supply, a lack of power across an area.

clue.text: Threaten target of the Luddites

definitions.meaning: to threaten is to appear menacingly, as storm clouds do
Luddites smashed the weaving machines that were taking their jobs

explanation.definitionFit: Trouble can hang menacingly overhead, and the weaving frame was what the Luddites, early nineteenth-century English textile workers, destroyed.

clue.text: Dog eats food

parts.note: eats is slang for food, as is chow
chow is slang for food

explanation.surface: A dog tucks into its dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'eats' and 'food' give the same slang word, CHOW; 'eats' looks like a verb but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The chow chow is a Chinese breed with a blue-black tongue.

clue.text: Old, wise tribe

parts.note: a sage person is wise

explanation.surface: An ancient and learned people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Osage are a Native American nation of the Great Plains.

clue.text: Author lost novel, then play

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of lost are arranged in a new way

parts.note: to toy with something is to play with it

explanation.surface: A writer misplaced his novel and then took to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges LOST to TOLS; 'novel' pretends to be a book, apt for this writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian novelist wrote War and Peace and Anna Karenina.

clue.text: Unknown figure in retro number

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the whole run of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: in algebra y is an unknown quantity
a figure is a number, such as ten

explanation.surface: A mysterious digit appears in an old-fashioned song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retro' turns Y + TEN + IN as one run, giving NI + NET + Y; 'number' looks like a song but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the whole number that follows eighty-nine.

clue.text: Single line on gold put in post

indicators.note: put in means placed inside the post synonym

parts.note: post is mail, letters delivered
taken as written
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A lone line of something golden is slipped into the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' splits the post word after its first letter. OR is the heraldic term for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway running on one rail, a single track, is a monorail.

clue.text: Unchecked article blocking path of aircraft

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the way, inside the aircraft path

parts.note: planes take off and land along a runway
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item left unattended is obstructing the airstrip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' places A inside RUNWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unchecked is out of control, like a runaway horse or train.

clue.text: Range of crumpets a dog's dinner?

indicators.note: a dog's dinner is British slang for a mess, so the letters of crumpets are jumbled

explanation.surface: A selection of teatime crumpets turns out to be a messy meal for the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a dog's dinner' (British for a mess) jumbles CRUMPETS; crumpets are British griddle cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a full range, as in the spectrum of opinion.

clue.text: Mark has posted tool we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: a tool that has been posted is an axe sent

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a tool has been mailed.
explanation.walkthrough: AXE SENT, from 'posted tool', said out loud matches the answer, signalled by 'we hear'.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent is a written mark over a letter, like the acute in café.

clue.text: Destination of meal for bear

definitions.meaning: food ends up in the belly after swallowing
to bear something is to tolerate it

explanation.definitionFit: Swallowed food goes to the belly, and to put up with something is to be able to take it.

clue.text: Bird — gull

definitions.meaning: a crow-family bird that nests in colonies
to gull someone is to cheat or deceive them

explanation.definitionFit: It is a black crow-like bird, and to cheat or swindle someone is to fleece them.

clue.text: Love of food is good, looking up?

parts.note: the science of studying the stars is literally looking up at the sky

explanation.surface: A sense of optimism, of things improving, is welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking up' seems to mean improving, but here is a playful description of stargazing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastronomy is the appreciation of fine cooking and eating.

clue.text: Frank behind move to take trick

parts.note: frank means open, done in plain view
behind is a noun here, the backside or rump

explanation.surface: A man named Frank lurks behind a move that wins the card game trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name but means open; 'behind' looks like a position but is the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games, to play a higher trump than one already played wins the trick.

clue.text: City women practising spelling test

parts.note: a group of witches casting spells is a coven
to try something is to test it

explanation.surface: An urban school sets a spelling test for women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelling' looks like orthography but means casting spells. COVENTRY is a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a city in the West Midlands of England, famous for its cathedral.

clue.text: Shield for a mascot, in other words

indicators.note: in other words suggests the same letters rewritten as different words

explanation.surface: A team badge is chosen to stand for its mascot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in other words' rearranges FOR A MASCOT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldic arms are displayed on a shield, the escutcheon.

clue.text: The L of London, perhaps?

parts.note: the first letter of the city's name is written large, and the city itself is the seat of government

explanation.definitionFit: A word starting a name takes an upper-case letter, and London is the UK's seat of government; both senses fit.

clue.text: Look sound

explanation.definitionFit: A quick glance is a peek, and a small squeak, as from a chick, is also called this.

clue.text: In yew, we hear, sheltered by tree

indicators.note: sheltered by means held within the tree name

parts.note: a poplar is a tall tree

indicators.note: we hear means the word is taken by its pronunciation

parts.note: the tree name yew is pronounced like the letter U

explanation.surface: A tree shades another tree, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns 'yew' into the letter U, 'sheltered by' POPLAR. 'In' means fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in is fashionable, widely liked.

clue.text: Doctor secure, securing operation

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of secure are altered

explanation.surface: A physician makes something safe in a surgical procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reorders SECURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescue is a mission to save people and bring them to safety.

clue.text: A shade after eleven, flat out

parts.note: past means after, as in half past ten

indicators.note: out means the flat synonym is removed from eleven

parts.note: a flat surface is even

explanation.surface: Someone is tired after eleven at night, completely flat out.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking EVEN 'out' of ELEVEN leaves EL; 'flat out' looks like exhaustion.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale, soft colour is called a pastel shade.

clue.text: He remains calm as one breaks beds up

indicators.note: breaks means splits open the reversed beds word
in a down clue, up means the beds word reads from the bottom

parts.note: cots are small beds
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man keeps his cool while someone breaks the beds apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns COTS to STOC, and the I 'breaks' it before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic is a person who endures hardship without complaint.

clue.text: Men in bar showing attachment to the bottle

indicators.note: in puts the men word inside the bar synonym

parts.note: to bar is to stop
a crew is a group of men working together

explanation.surface: Men in a pub show they are fond of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub and 'attachment to the bottle' like a drinking habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cap that twists on to seal a bottle neck is a screw-top.

clue.text: Opposed to prayer without limits?

indicators.note: without limits means losing its first and last letters

parts.note: the praying mantis is jokingly called a prayer

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether one is against unlimited prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'prayer' here is one who prays: the praying MANTIS, which loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti as a word means against.

clue.text: Time going off, moving slowly

parts.note: food going off is rotting

explanation.surface: Time is passing as something goes slowly bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' looks like departing but means decaying.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that trots goes at a gait slower than a canter.

clue.text: True account, short shory about university

indicators.note: about means the trimmed story goes round the university letter
short means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A real tale is told about a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts TALE to TAL, which goes 'about' U.
explanation.definitionFit: Something actual is real and genuine.

clue.text: Courageous going topless to swim, as fair game

indicators.note: going topless means losing the first letter

parts.note: plucky means brave
a dip is a swim

explanation.surface: A brave soul goes topless for a swim in a show of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' removes the P of PLUCKY. A lucky dip is a fairground game of pulling a prize from a tub.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub prize game at a fair, where you draw a hidden gift, is a lucky dip.

clue.text: Spray — with this in riot?

parts.note: a stinging aerosol named after a hot seasoning is used by police at disorderly crowds

explanation.definitionFit: Pepper spray is the irritant police use for crowd control, so the seasoning completes the phrase.
